overall_summary: Analysis of FACTVERSE performance data shows that high-concept space and extreme exoplanet scenarios (particularly 'What If You Fell Into...' hooks and surreal planetary environments like diamond, burning ice, and dark planets) are driving the strongest views-per-day and engagement (likes-per-view). In contrast, older or more standard psychological and basic biology facts published earlier in September are underperforming in daily velocity. Recent uploads focusing on interactive spatial hypotheticals achieve superior traction.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Darkest Planet?' (YlDuGu1vzAg) generated over 1,000 and 825 views rapidly with high like ratios.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on 'What If You Fell Into...' formatting applied to extreme, newly researched cosmic bodies.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles detailing bizarre weather or physical properties ('The Planet Darker Than Coal', 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!') consistently outperform standard science facts.
winning_patterns.action: Produce more short-form deep dives into bizarre astronomical phenomena with visceral, sensory adjectives (supersonic, molten, absolute zero).

weak_patterns.evidence: Recycled topics or standard facts about human memory ('Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories') and basic animal trivia ('Octopuses Have Three Hearts') stalled out with minimal daily view growth in recent weeks.
weak_patterns.action: Pause standard psychological micro-facts unless paired with a high-stakes narrative or thriller-grade framing.

next_video.concept: Surviving inside a rogue planet ejected from its solar system wandering through eternal interstellar darkness.
next_video.opening_direction: Start with total sensory deprivation: absolute zero temperatures freezing air instantly, forcing the viewer to imagine total isolation trillion of miles from any star.
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that despite having no sun, the planet's core is sustained by colossal tidal friction, creating glowing subterranean magma oceans beneath miles of ice.
next_video.reason: Capitalizes on the proven high-performing 'What If' exoplanet and dark-planet formats while introducing a fresh, unexplored cosmic concept (rogue planets with internal magma oceans).
